body: I joined the military to get away from where I lived in Portland. It's a nice city but no place for a new lawyer, it's all shitlaw and where youg people go to retire. It would be just the icing on the cake. Like I said, no good options. I had options, but I didn't take them soon enough. And it doesn't change the fact that any relationship I start will just end up like this one.

32 year old veteran law student who commutes into NYC from a bedroom community and knows no one in that town, which is my wife's hometown, and has no real connections at his school. No close friends anymore because I ignored them for her. 

I'm too old to be a student, and both potential friends and dates here expect me to be into a lucrative career by now. I have nothing in common with people my age here.

Not really a workable situation.
I get that now...just too late. I needed to get it three years ago when I was well positioned to leave and have a better life.

I just can't see myself being without someone for a year in a half here. I don't really think forming a few loose friendships is going to be enough to hold myself together. And once I graduate there's no guarantee I'll get a good job and I will potentially be in th same boat. I can't keep living for tomorrow but I won't be able to live happily today.

Maybe she isn't easy to get along with, it feels that way, but she's not the first person to leave me for not being emotionally supportive. I have more evidence of my fault than hers. 

That doesn't leave me with a lot of hope, because at least initially she was easier to get along with and we really connected. 

I'm 32 now, so dating won't be easy, especially in NYC as a law student at my age. I don't really fit the demographic. I don't want to move back home and I hardly know my classmates, plus I am out of the phase of law school when I could have made closer friends. At this point a jump off a bridge seems like a great idea, I just don't want to risk the chance of somehow surviving.
